notes:
Residents: INSEE Filosofi 2021, a 200m uniform population grid covering all of metropolitan France (total population including children and retirees) -- already fine-grained, nothing further to place.

Jobs: total counts per commune come from INSEE MOBPRO 2021, a full national commune-to-commune commute survey covering where people actually work (place of work, not employer registration). For placement WITHIN each destination commune, we moved beyond population-density placement (used on our other France maps) to real establishment-level data: INSEE's SIRENE business register, specifically the official "Géolocalisation des établissements du répertoire SIRENE" dataset (INSEE, updated monthly) joined to "StockEtablissement" for employee-count brackets and activity codes. We kept only active employer establishments (excluding non-employing/closed units), weighted each by the midpoint of its employee-count bracket, and snapped each to the nearest real building footprint (Overture Maps buildings, open dataset -- not IGN's official cadastral layer, disclosed here for transparency) within 100m (99.7% of establishments snapped successfully; ~0.3% kept their raw geocoded SIRENE coordinate). Within each commune, MOBPRO's real job total is then distributed across these real building-anchored establishment points weighted by their SIRENE employee count, instead of being distributed across residential population cells -- densities are directly tuned to match MOBPRO's real per-commune statistics by construction, since MOBPRO fixes the total and SIRENE only decides the real-world spatial distribution within it. This eliminates the "business district underrepresented" bias documented in our own pipeline notes (e.g. La Defense, where population-based placement previously required a hand-curated correction we have now removed since SIRENE naturally places jobs on the real office towers).

Commute flows: full MOBPRO commune-to-commune matrix (~219k origin-destination pairs kept for this map's extended bounding box), not estimated. Minimum-distance floor of 10km applied to synthetic pop generation with a spatial fallback for structurally small communes (median resulting commute: 27km / 32min, consistent with a large multi-department region). Routing via local OSRM, traffic congestion multiplier (1.55x, among the most congested metros in Europe) applied to trips >=3km.

Map coverage: extended well beyond Ile-de-France's administrative boundary to include every town where an RER or Transilien line terminates, even outside the region (Creil and Crepy-en-Valois in Oise, Chateau-Thierry and La Ferte-Milon in Aisne, Gisors and Vernon in Eure, Dreux in Eure-et-Loir, Montargis in Loiret) -- verified against each line's actual current terminus, not assumed from the administrative region alone. — Reviewer refinements (2026-08-23): workplace resolution scored ml_hybrid_footprints, not exact_footprints — the author discloses (twice) that footprints are Overture, not the IGN cadastre, and 99.7% of SIRENE establishments are snapped ONTO those footprints, so the final placement geometry is Overture (the rubric R-ladder names Overture as the ml_hybrid example). The SIRENE contribution — employee-bracket weights constrained to MOBPRO per-commune totals by construction — is intensity-side and fully credited at fine_types_calibrated. Resident resolution pinned to mesh_250 (Filosofi is a 200m grid). Upgrade path noted for the author: re-snapping to IGN BD TOPO official footprints would lift R to exact_footprints and the map to high.
